regions.name: Lagos
regions.story: Home turf. If your name rings from Ikeja to Epe, the whole country will hear it.

regions.name: South-West
regions.story: One expressway from Lagos: big cities, busy markets and customers who love a party.

regions.name: South-South
regions.story: Port cities and oil-town salaries: customers here pay well for quality.

regions.name: South-East
regions.story: Giant trading markets and factories: win the traders here and stock moves fast.

regions.name: North-Central + Abuja
regions.story: The capital and the food basket: steady office money and the road to the north.

regions.name: North-West
regions.story: Centuries-old trade routes and the most people of any zone: volume is king here.

regions.name: North-East
regions.story: The last zone: finish here and your brand is in all 36 states plus Abuja.

regions.name: West Africa
regions.story: First border crossing: follow the coast road and your export trucks become shops.

regions.name: Rest of Africa
regions.story: From Douala to Cape Town: a truly continental brand, one capital city at a time.

regions.name: UK + Europe
regions.story: Diaspora customers miss home badly. They pay in pounds and euros for a taste of it.

regions.name: North America
regions.story: Dollar market: huge diaspora cities where one branch earns like ten back home.

regions.name: Middle East + Asia
regions.story: The final frontier: store number 500 opens here and the sun never sets on you.

phases.name: Roadside Hustle
phases.playerGoal: Grow the flagship from roadside stall to a proper shop and survive the first month-end.
phases.hook: Tomorrow's event is teased tonight, and the next renovation is always one good day away.

phases.name: Flagship Boss
phases.playerGoal: Finish the flagship ladder: mega venue, car, house and a full, paid team.
phases.hook: A truck is booked for tomorrow morning: stock up tonight or miss the bulk order.

phases.name: Lagos Takeover
phases.playerGoal: Open all 20 Lagos branches and fill supermarket and hotel contracts.
newThings: Branches open one at a time
phases.hook: Branches keep earning while you sleep: open the app to collect and place the next one.

phases.name: Southern Conquest
phases.playerGoal: Plant 115 branches across South-West, South-South and South-East.
phases.hook: Each state capital you open lights up the map, and the next one is already half paid for.

phases.name: One Nigeria
phases.playerGoal: Cover Abuja and the three northern zones: all 36 states plus the capital.
phases.hook: The map shows how many states are left. Nobody stops at 31 out of 37.

phases.name: ECOWAS Express
phases.playerGoal: Cross the border: 60 West Africa branches, then 50 more across the continent.
phases.hook: A new country unlocks every few days, each with a bigger first-week opening bonus.

phases.name: Diaspora Dream
phases.playerGoal: Open in the UK, Europe and North America where homesick customers pay top price.
phases.hook: Containers take days to land: come back to see it dock and cash out the big cheque.

phases.name: Global Legend
phases.playerGoal: Open store 500 in Asia, appoint the Group CEO and reach day 1,000.
phases.hook: A countdown to store 500 and day 1,000 sits on screen. You are too close to stop now.

commonEvents.name: Fuel Scarcity
commonEvents.text: Queue at every filling station. Delivery van is crawling today.

commonEvents.name: Heavy Rain
commonEvents.text: Rain don start since morning. Customers are hiding under umbrellas.

commonEvents.name: Salary Week
commonEvents.text: Alert don enter! Workers are spending like tomorrow no dey.

commonEvents.name: Detty December
commonEvents.text: Returnees have landed with strong currency and big appetite.

commonEvents.name: Power Cut
commonEvents.text: Light don go. Generator is drinking diesel like zobo.

commonEvents.name: Owambe Weekend
commonEvents.text: Three parties on one street. Aso-ebi crowd wants bulk orders.

commonEvents.name: Public Holiday
commonEvents.text: Independence Day! Everybody is outside and ready to enjoy.

commonEvents.name: Market Sanitation Day
commonEvents.text: Sweep first, sell later. Shop opens late after the clean-up.

commonEvents.name: Go-Slow on the Bridge
commonEvents.text: Truck break down for bridge. Supplies will reach when they reach.

commonEvents.name: Customer Went Viral
commonEvents.text: One happy customer posted you online. Phones are ringing nonstop!

commonEvents.name: Ajo Payout
commonEvents.text: It is your turn to collect the thrift contribution. Sweet alert!

commonEvents.name: Staff Sharp Sharp
commonEvents.text: Everybody resumed early and in good mood. Work is flying today.

traffic: Conductor: Oshodi! Oshodi! Hold your change o!
Hawker: Gala! Cold pure water! Plantain chips!
LASTMA officer is watching. Stay on your lane.
Pothole ahead. Car is doing shaku shaku.
Danfo squeezed in front. Madam just sighed.
Third Mainland: 2 km in 40 minutes. Normal.
Okada passed between two trailers. Na wa o.
Boy selling phone chargers runs beside the car
Keke horn sounds like an angry goat.
Trailer park for road at Mile 2. We wait.
radio: DJ Sabi: This go-slow jam na for you!
Now playing: 'Jollof for Two' by Lady Zobo
Traffic report: everywhere red. Stay strong.
Next up: 'My Alert Don Enter' by Baba Credit
Caller: I left work at 5, I still dey Ikeja!
Oldie: 'Sweet Like Boli' by The Suya Kings
You dey listen to Go-Slow FM, 99.9 patience
Fresh one: 'Generator Lullaby' by Mama NEPA
dinner: Pounded yam and egusi. Phone on silent.
Jollof rice, fried plantain and cold zobo.
Amala and ewedu with plenty assorted meat.
Hot pepper soup to chase the traffic away.
Beans and dodo. Simple, sweet, correct.
Eba and okra soup, eaten in happy silence.
bath: Bucket of warm water. Today's stress dey go.
Singing in the bathroom like a superstar.
Tap is rushing tonight. Small miracle!
Scrubbing off market dust and traffic smoke.
sleep: Fan on, wrapper up. Counting naira, not sheep.
Alarm set for 5:30. Tomorrow we go again.
morning: Cock crow before alarm. No snooze for boss.
Quick stretch, then check yesterday's sales.
Hot tea, bread and fried egg. Fuel for hustle.
Tie the gele sharp. Boss must look like boss.
Akara woman already frying outside. Buy 200.
Keys, phone, cashbook. Shop opens at 8!

managerRoles.title: Shop Manager
managerRoles.unlockAt: Flagship level 20, before the first branch
managerRoles.does: Runs the flagship while you are away: restocks, serves and banks cash at 60% efficiency.

managerRoles.title: Area Manager
managerRoles.unlockAt: When you open the 5th Lagos branch
managerRoles.does: Collects profit from every Lagos branch automatically and cuts their running costs by 10%.

managerRoles.title: Regional Manager
managerRoles.unlockAt: First branch in any new region (one per region)
managerRoles.does: Lets branches open in that region and lifts their daily profit by 15%.

managerRoles.title: General Manager
managerRoles.unlockAt: 100 branches and all southern regions open
managerRoles.does: Opens the next branch for you when cash allows and pays salaries and tax on time.

managerRoles.title: Group CEO
managerRoles.does: Doubles offline earnings and lifts profit of every store worldwide by 20%.

retention.psychology: Money that piles up while away makes every return feel like a reward and absence feel like waste.
retention.inGame: Branches and managers earn overnight; a 'While you slept' cheque greets you, capped until the next manager.

retention.psychology: Loss aversion: people protect a streak they have built more fiercely than they chase a new prize.
retention.inGame: 7-day 'Market Week' calendar ending in a big Saturday bonus; one missed day is forgiven by the Shop Manager.

retention.psychology: The goal-gradient effect: effort rises the closer a finish line looks, so one must always be close.
retention.inGame: The map shows the next city greyed out with a progress bar for its cost, plus region and store-500 counters.

retention.psychology: A scheduled payoff gives a concrete reason and a time to reopen the app.
retention.inGame: Export trucks and overseas containers arrive at a stated time; stock the bay before then to earn in full.

retention.psychology: Unpredictable rewards stay exciting far longer than fixed ones; curiosity pulls players into the next day.
retention.inGame: One random event per day, hinted at on the night radio, so each morning plays a little differently.

retention.psychology: A regular scorecard gives closure and a personal best to beat next time.
retention.inGame: Every 30 days: sales, salaries, tax and net profit with a grade and a 'beat last month' target.

retention.psychology: Unfinished sets nag at people; filling the last gap is deeply satisfying.
retention.inGame: State capitals, country flags and region stamps fill a passport book; full regions give a permanent profit boost.

retention.psychology: Novelty resets boredom; a new toy every few sessions keeps the core loop feeling fresh.
retention.inGame: Machines, contract tiers, manager ranks and regions are spaced so something new opens every 10 to 20 days.

retention.psychology: Limited-time moments create urgency and something to anticipate long in advance.
retention.inGame: Salary week every month and Detty December every game year bring price spikes worth preparing stock for.

retention.psychology: Visible status and a personal rise from nothing make progress feel like identity, not just numbers.
retention.inGame: Her title, car, house and night routine upgrade from roadside trader to Group Chairman as the empire grows.

sources.claim: Nigeria has six geopolitical zones (North-Central, North-East, North-West, South-East, South-South, South-West) covering the 36 states and the FCT; used for region grouping and state capitals.
Zone-by-zone list of Nigerian states used to cross-check that every state capital appears in its region.
London, especially south-east areas such as Peckham, is a centre of the British Nigerian community.
Houston and other large US metro areas host the biggest Nigerian communities in the United States.
The Oshodi-Apapa expressway and Mile 2 axis are notorious Lagos gridlock points, often blocked by trucks.
Lagos areas with the heaviest traffic, used for the go-slow night lines.
Idle games retain players through offline earnings, regular new content, events and clear long-term goals.
Long-running idle games rely on live events and layered progression for multi-year retention.
